title: RFK Jr. headlines sold-out anti-vaccine conference alongside Andrew Wakefield
gist: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. will keynote a sold-out September 17 Children's Health Defense conference in Washington alongside Andrew Wakefield, the delicensed author of the retracted MMR-autism study. Ars reads this as Kennedy abandoning the 'pro-vaccine' framing he used at his confirmation hearing and openly embracing anti-vaccine advocacy — a shift arriving shortly after reports that President Trump pressed him to aggressively pursue the vaccines-cause-autism claim.

themes.theme: A sitting health secretary openly rejoins the movement

insights.claim: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. will deliver the keynote at an anti-vaccine conference in Washington, DC hosted by Children's Health Defense, the organization he once led and cofounded.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The cabinet official controlling US vaccine policy publicly aligning with an advocacy group signals regulatory risk for vaccine makers beyond rhetoric.

insights.claim: Kennedy formally separated from Children's Health Defense when he took the health secretary role around the start of 2025 and repeatedly claimed at his confirmation hearing that he is 'pro-vaccine' despite a lengthy record as an anti-vaccine activist.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Establishes the baseline commitment against which this appearance is a measurable reversal — useful for handicapping how far policy will move from stated positions.

insights.claim: Ars Technica assesses Kennedy's decision to headline a starkly anti-vaccine event as a shift toward openly embracing his ideology and agenda rather than continuing to distance himself.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: An open shift in posture typically precedes concrete administrative action — watch ACIP composition, schedule revisions and CDC guidance as the follow-through.
insights.quote: Kennedy’s decision to headline a starkly anti-vaccine event appears to be a shift toward openly embracing his ideology and agenda.
insights.locator: Kennedy's decision to headline a starkly anti-vaccine event

insights.claim: The shift follows shortly after reports that President Trump urged Kennedy to aggressively pursue the falsehood that vaccines cause autism.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Presidential backing removes the main political constraint on HHS action — raises the probability of formal federal moves against established vaccine schedules.
insights.locator: That shift comes shortly after reports that President Trump has urged Kennedy

themes.theme: Wakefield's rehabilitation inside US health politics

insights.claim: Andrew Wakefield, stripped of his medical license over a fraudulent and retracted study falsely linking autism to the MMR vaccine, is appearing on the same program as the sitting US health secretary.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Platforming a discredited researcher at a government-adjacent event marks a normalization threshold that erodes the evidentiary basis of US vaccine regulation.
insights.locator: Kennedy will appear alongside other high-profile figures

insights.claim: A medical board investigation found that Wakefield had mistreated vulnerable children and that his actions amounted to serious professional misconduct, yet he has remained an enduring figure in the anti-vaccine community.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Demonstrates that professional sanction has no durable deplatforming effect once a claim attaches to an identity movement — misinformation risk does not decay on its own.
insights.locator: An investigation by a medical board found that Wakefield had mistreated vulnerable children

insights.claim: The conference registration site describes Wakefield as a 'tireless advocate for parental choice' and Kennedy as 'a uniquely powerful and celebrated champion for those whose voices have long gone unheard.'
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The 'parental choice' framing is the movement's mainstreaming vector — it converts a scientific dispute into a rights argument that is far harder to counter politically.
insights.locator: The online registration site for the CHD's conference

insights.claim: Children's Health Defense and Kennedy have provided significant help in sustaining the false vaccines-cause-autism claim by embracing and widely promoting the link.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific distribution channel that kept the claim alive — a template for how organized advocacy sustains claims after retraction.
insights.locator: His dangerous falsehood that vaccines cause autism has also endured

themes.theme: The 'health freedom' coalition and its commercial base

insights.claim: The September 17 conference is billed as a 'pursuit of a more perfect future' addressing the risks and opportunities for the 'health freedom movement,' with an opening reception the night before.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The 'health freedom' label is the umbrella under which vaccine, food and pharma deregulation agendas are being bundled — a broader policy surface than vaccines alone.
insights.quote: pursuit of a more perfect future

insights.claim: The speaker roster spans sitting senators Ron Johnson and Rand Paul, MAHA Institute president Mark Gorton, Epoch Times senior editor Jan Jekielek, and CHD CEO Mary Holland — a coalition of legislative, institutional and media actors rather than fringe activists alone.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Senate participation means this agenda has a legislative channel, not only an executive one — watch for hearings and appropriations riders targeting vaccine programs.
insights.locator: Other speakers on the agenda include

insights.claim: In-person tickets priced at $250 sold out, with limited main-room seating still available at $125 and livestream access at $100, indicating real paying demand rather than a subsidized event.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A sold-out $250 ticket is a hard measure of the movement's monetizable audience — the funding base that sustains sustained pressure on health agencies.
insights.locator: In-person tickets to the conference, priced at $250, are sold out
